label: Cohort prefill admission
mechanism: arrivals pool until a retiring cohort actually frees slots, then prefill together as ONE right-padded group — filling the native MMA's 128-row expert M tile that a single sequence leaves ~87% empty
hypothesis: The accepted engine (exp-0016 prefill + exp-0015b decode, ledger iter 18 @ 194.5 tok/s) runs routed experts on the native NVFP4xNVFP4 grouped MMA, which pads every expert group to a 128-row M tile: an expert's GEMM cost is FLAT from 1 to 128 rows. One canonical prompt (T~745, top-6 over 256 experts) routes only ~17 rows to each expert, so prefill pays a nearly-empty tile per expert per layer — and it pays it once PER SEQUENCE, which the cycle model puts at 911 x 0.3805 s = 347 s of the 600 s box (58%). Co-prefilling a cohort fills the tile that is already paid for. The batched walk itself is exp-0014's, cherry-picked verbatim (right-padded groups, stable length-sort, partitioned under the 4 GiB padded-scores budget, per-row state seeding through the unchanged per-seq seed/append calls, causality isolating real rows from pads, singleton fall-through); exp-0014 was rejected not on that machinery but because its 150 ms wall-clock accumulation window raced per-completion HTTP arrivals and admitted mostly singletons (its DEADENDS post-mortem: grouping must be triggered by the scheduler's own cohort-retire signal). ONE variable changes here: EngineLoop pools arrivals and releases them when (a) nothing is generating — sequential singletons, i.e. the D13 gate, cold start and drain tails keep the batch-1-exact per-seq path and never stall; (b) PREFILL_COHORT=6 prompts have gathered AND >= 6 slots are free, i.e. a cohort actually retired and made room, never releasing more than the free slots (a request the scheduler cannot admit now would sit in waiting and be admitted alone later); or (c) a 4 s valve. A released cohort prefills as one group, decodes in lockstep and retires together, so its replacements co-arrive and the structure is self-sustaining after one round. GPU evidence on GPUs 4-7 (t_prefill_batch_exp0017_warm_out.log, one resident load, N=64 canonical-ISL prompts): warm serial 380.5 ms/seq vs grouped 201.7 ms/seq = 1.89x on the prefill term (the cold serial arm reads 4.25x, but 56% of it is first-call CUTE DSL / Triton / cuBLAS JIT the steady-state bench never re-pays — the honest ratio is the warm one, and its 380.5 ms/seq independently matches the ~370 ms/seq the accepted 194.5 tok/s row implies). Two-point fit (per-seq = A/G + B, A = 183.7 ms flat, B = 196.8 ms scaling) gives 1.67x at the G=6 target, and the modelled throughput plateau is flat over G in 6..12 once rows held out of the B-independent graphed decode step are charged. Determinism: G == G2 bitwise on tokens AND fp32 logit rows at the prefill seam; Scheduler.step() stays a pure function of its input schedule (wall clock enters only through the valve), so the t_b3 same-schedule arm is untouched. D13 teacher-forced gate GREEN and bitwise identical to the accepted exp-0016/0015b numbers (0.9475 / 0.043856 / 0.396472) — release rule (a) keeps the sequential gate on the unchanged path, which also proves the pool cannot stall a sequential client. Carried alongside as measurement hygiene at the exp-0014 post-mortem's explicit request, and incapable of speeding up a served request: HTTP listen backlog 5 -> 256, the artifact that dropped 3 of 64 bench threads and cost exp-0014 -4% of its headline.
predicted_delta: +25-37% timeboxed decode_heavy tok/s: 245-267 vs the best same-protocol accepted row 194.5 (merge bar 195.1). Cycle model on that row: 600 s box / conc 64 / osl 128 = 911 requests, prefill 911 x 0.3805 s = 347 s (58%) + decode 253 s; at G=6 the measured 1.67x takes prefill to ~208 s while holding ~3 of 64 rows out of the graphed step lifts decode to ~265 s -> ~473 s of work in the same box. Floor case: if the bench's arrival pattern still fragments groups, admissions stay singletons on the unchanged per-seq path and the number lands back at ~194.5 — which is itself the measurement that closes out the batched-prefill line for good.
